pointers.sentence: The admin's forms use the widgets of `django/contrib/admin/widgets.py`: its own inputs for dates, times, text, numbers, URLs, files and UUIDs; `RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper`, with links to add, change, delete and view a related object; the raw-id widgets `ForeignKeyRawIdWidget` and `ManyToManyRawIdWidget`; and `AutocompleteSelect`, whose script asks `AutocompleteJsonView` for matching rows as the user types.

`BaseModelAdmin.__init__` merges `formfield_overrides` into a copy of `FORMFIELD_FOR_DBFIELD_DEFAULTS`, and `formfield_for_dbfield` searches the result along a model field's MRO, so a ship's tonnage, a `PositiveIntegerField`, takes the entry for `IntegerField` ([The admin's forms: `get_form` and `formfield_for_dbfield`](admin-forms.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:FORMFIELD_FOR_DBFIELD_DEFAULTS`, `django/db/models/fields/__init__.py`, `django/db/models/fields/files.py`).

| `DateField`, `TimeField` | `AdminDateWidget`, `AdminTimeWidget` | `"vDateField"`, `"vTimeField"`: a calendar, a clock (`django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/admin/DateTimeShortcuts.js`) |

Each takes the first that applies: a widget passed in, as `formfield_overrides` passes one for a field's exact class; an autocomplete widget for a field `BaseModelAdmin.get_autocomplete_fields` names; a raw-id widget for one in `BaseModelAdmin.raw_id_fields`; then `AdminRadioSelect` for a foreign key in `BaseModelAdmin.radio_fields`, or `FilteredSelectMultiple` for a many-to-many field in `BaseModelAdmin.filter_horizontal` or `filter_vertical`; otherwise the model field's own select (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_manytomany`).

`formfield_for_dbfield` gives it the related model admin's answers for the request to `has_add_permission`, `has_change_permission`, `has_delete_permission` and `has_view_permission`, and no link for a model not registered on the site (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_dbfield`).

The wrapper drops change, delete and view beside anything but a select of one value, and delete for a relation whose `on_delete` is `CASCADE`, where a comment calls the deletion confusing (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper.__init__`).

`"__fk__"` marks where the key goes, which `"RelatedObjectLookups.js"`, a script of `ModelAdmin.media`, fills in when the page loads and whenever the select changes (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper.get_context`, `django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/admin/RelatedObjectLookups.js`).

The add or change form there carries the three keys on as hidden inputs, and an addition ends in the popup branch of `ModelAdmin.response_add`: no success message and no redirect, but the new object's value for `"_to_field"` and its text, as JSON, in the template `"admin/popup_response.html"` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.response_add`). piet added a port from home's add link:

The answer's script calls a function of the opening window, which adds Naples to home's select and selects it, or writes the key into a raw-id input, and closes the popup (`django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/admin/RelatedObjectLookups.js`).

`ForeignKeyRawIdWidget` adds a link to the related model's change list, if that model is registered, and the current object's text, found by one query and, for a registered model, linked to its change page (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:ForeignKeyRawIdWidget.get_context`). home, in a model admin made by hand with `raw_id_fields = ["home"]`:
The lookup link opens the change list in a popup, where a click on a row writes its value for `"_to_field"` into the input (`django/contrib/admin/templatetags/admin_list.py:items_for_result`).

`ManyToManyRawIdWidget` holds keys separated by commas, with no text and no `"_to_field"`, and a key chosen is appended (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:ManyToManyRawIdWidget`, `django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/admin/RelatedObjectLookups.js`).

`ManyToManyRawIdWidget` holds keys separated by commas, with no text and no `"_to_field"`, and a key chosen is appended (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:ManyToManyRawIdWidget`, `django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/admin/RelatedObjectLookups.js`).
A relation's `limit_choices_to`, if a dictionary, goes into the link's query string too (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:url_params_from_lookup_dict`).

`BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed` refuses a lookup across a relation that neither a filter nor the date hierarchy offers, but first admits any lookup and value a foreign key to the model has in its `limit_choices_to`, so that, its comment says, these popups work (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.lookup_allowed`).

`AdminRadioSelect` serves a foreign key or a field with choices named in `radio_fields`, with the class `"radiolist"` for `VERTICAL` or `"radiolist inline"` for `HORIZONTAL`; beside a foreign key's buttons the wrapper shows at most the add link (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:get_ul_class`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_choice_field`).

`FilteredSelectMultiple` is a multiple select that `"SelectFilter2.js"` turns into two filtered boxes, available and chosen, side by side for `filter_horizontal` and stacked for `filter_vertical`, keeping, since 6.1, named groups of choices as optgroups; the script, the widget's docstring warns, needs the JavaScript catalogue (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:FilteredSelectMultiple`, `django/contrib/admin/static/admin/js/SelectBox.js`, `docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

The widget draws only the selected options, found by one query if any, and a blank one for an optional single select (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:AutocompleteMixin.optgroups`), and writes in attributes what Select2 needs to fetch the rest: the URL of the site's autocomplete view; the application, model and name of the field being edited; and a `"lang"`, the active language as Select2 names it, whose translation the widget's media add to jQuery and Select2 (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:AutocompleteMixin.build_attrs`, `django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:get_select2_language`).

`process_request` reads `"term"`, `"app_label"`, `"model_name"` and `"field_name"`, and answers 403 unless the last three lead to a relation whose model is registered on the site, since, its docstring says, the permission check needs that model's admin; 404 if that model admin's `get_search_fields` gives no fields; and 403 if the relation's target field fails `to_field_allowed` (`django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py:AutocompleteJsonView.process_request`).

Then it asks that model admin's `has_view_permission`, takes its queryset, narrows it by `limit_choices_to`, searches it with `get_search_results` ([Filters and search: `list_filter`, `search_fields` and `date_hierarchy`](filters.md)), and pages it twenty rows at a time (`django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py:AutocompleteJsonView.get`, `django/contrib/admin/views/autocomplete.py:AutocompleteJsonView.get_queryset`).

It guards the related model, which a user must be allowed to view so that, the documentation says, its rows are not disclosed (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/index.txt`).
